documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release
Audited Financial Results For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its Q4 and full year FY26 financial and operational results, achieving its highest ever annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and record production volumes across multiple petroleum products. The company maintained a strong financial position with a low net debt-equity ratio of 0.09 and announced a total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year, alongside planning future capex initiatives including Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS projects and retail outlets. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its Q4 FY25 financial and operational performance, highlighting a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for the year and 2.974 MMT in Q4. The company's annual GRM stood at $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 in the previous year, primarily driven by lower international product cracks. Management discussed maintenance schedules, opportunity crude sourcing, maintenance and value-added project capex plans, and the ongoing Cauvery basin refinery project developments.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor Spirit demand in the southern market shows a growth projection of around 4% to 5%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%.

demand_outlook.claim: High-speed diesel growth forecast in the southern market is projected at 3%.
demand_outlook.quote: HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor Spirit has a clear shortfall in the southern market where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has all approvals in place for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project, and project execution has started in full swing.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor for which 300 licenses were taken has started, and commissioning will occur during the financial year.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The capex for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project is INR 1,600 crores and the retail outlet project is INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The normal annual capex is estimated at another INR 500 crores every year.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: Total capex spent during the financial year was Rs. 673 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: Maintenance capex is expected to remain in the range of Rs. 200-250 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the CBR project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CBR update, in the last year we revised the capital cost as well as the capital structure. The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for the fourth quarter was reported at $10.3 per barrel.
Foreign exchange loss for the quarter was approximately INR 200 crores and for the whole year was around INR 350 crores.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: Full year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: Quarter 4 GRM was $6.22 per barrel compared to $7.7 per barrel in the same quarter of the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel. Again, if I compare the previous year same quarter, it was $7.7 per barrel, but if I compare it to Singapore benchmark, which was only $3.1 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported GRM of $11.91/bbl for 2022-23, $8.64/bbl for 2023-24, and $3.40/bbl for 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, which is equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In quarter 4, the company achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The new Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS unit capacity will be a fresh addition of 250,000 KTPA.
orders_capacity.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capital_allocation.claim: The gross leverage debt-equity stands at 0.18 compared to 0.39 last year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: On a gross basis, borrowings are INR 1,900 crores, while on a net basis, it is INR 973 crores with a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: Capital expenditure for the current year was INR 856 crores compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Debt-to-equity position as of March 31, 2025, stands at 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Total debt stood at Rs. 3,100 crores and net worth stood at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024. Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to operations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the INR 2,000 crores total capex for LOBS and retail outlets will happen over the next 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Maintenance capex for the next two years is projected to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores without additional projects.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
